speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the reason for the delay in the roll-out of distance-based charging in the next-generation ERP system (ERP2) despite this being a key feature and cost component; (b) what is the timeline for the implementation of distance-based charging; and (c) how much of the $556 million ERP2 contract was spent on this feature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It will remove the need to maintain the current bulky gantries and generate accurate real time traffic data to support transport policy, planning and traffic management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Member asked about the timeline for implementing distance-based charging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The current approach is point-based or cordon pricing – vehicles are charged when they cross a specific point or a cordon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Give the nexgen ERP system some time to settle down first.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In the meantime, we will study different approaches and options.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: First, will the distance-based charging – when it is rolled out eventually – be revenue neutral for the Government, compared to the current ERP system?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And if so, will we expect a reduction in road tax once the distance-based charging is rolled out?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am also concerned about how distance-based charging may impact individuals who drive or ride to work like taxi drivers or private hire drivers or delivery riders.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, will there be concessionary distance charging rates for these groups?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And lastly, will coupon-less charging for roadside parking, be rolled out in the first phase of this new system?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, the reason why we have rolled out nexgen ERP is because there is a need to replace the current system, which is nearing the end of its operational life.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And when we evaluated various technologies, it was found that GNSS was the most appropriate technology given that we will then be able to do away with bulky gantries, which occupy road space and also be able to avoid, for instance, the need for manpower intensive maintenance of these gantries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, this technology based on GNSS will be able to give us accurate, real-time traffic data, which will help us to do even better in terms of transport policy, planning and traffic management.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have noted, the system also has the capabilities for, and potentially we can implement, distance-based charging.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But, I think our current focus really is on ensuring that the installation process for the million or so motorists in Singapore, will take place as smoothly as possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to give the nexgen ERP time to settle and also to give us time to collect information on traffic patterns, travel patterns, distance travelled impact on the different types of motoristsand so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Then, we can study the different options and approaches, and come to a decision.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And in fact, it is already rolled out to many car parks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This system also has the capability to do that, but it is not a key feature nor a key criterion for us adopting this technology.
